en.title: Call of Duty YouTuber Petitions to Remove SBMM After Destiny Success
en.summary: A prominent Call of Duty YouTuber has launched a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking from unranked playlists, drawing inspiration from successful fan protests in Destiny. The move highlights ongoing community frustration with the system's impact on casual play.
en.body:
The debate surrounding skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) in **Call of Duty** has reached a new fever pitch, with YouTuber Tdawgsmitty spearheading a petition to remove it from unranked lobbies. Inspired by the recent fan success in rallying for changes in **Destiny 2**, Tdawgsmitty is leveraging community power to voice frustrations that many players share.

For years, **Call of Duty** players have debated the intricacies of its matchmaking, with SBMM often cited as a source of frustration. The system aims to create balanced matches by pairing players of similar skill levels. However, critics argue that in unranked modes, this creates a consistently high-pressure environment that detracts from the casual experience. Tdawgsmitty's petition points to statements from former developers, suggesting that the prioritization of SBMM over factors like player ping and region may have been influenced by data analysis and marketing strategies within Activision. The core argument is that while SBMM has a place in competitive ranked play, its presence in public matches can make it difficult to experiment with new weapons, relax after a long day, or simply play with friends of varying skill levels without facing relentlessly tough lobbies.

## Fan Frustration Mounts

The petition, which quickly garnered over 500 signatures within its first hour, reflects a deep-seated sentiment within the **Call of Duty** community. Many players feel that the current SBMM implementation transforms every public match into a high-stakes tournament, sapping the fun out of the game. This contrasts with the original intent of public matches, which were often seen as a space for less intense, more varied gameplay. The success of **Destiny 2** fans in influencing developer decisions has clearly emboldened Tdawgsmitty and others to believe that a similar outcome is possible for **Call of Duty**.

## What's Next for SBMM

Activision has historically maintained that SBMM is crucial for player retention and engagement, with internal data suggesting it leads to a better experience for a majority of players, particularly those with lower skill levels. While adjustments to SBMM are possible, a complete removal from all **Call of Duty** playlists seems unlikely given the company's stated reliance on the system for game health. Fans will be watching closely to see if this petition, or future community efforts, can prompt Activision to reconsider its approach to matchmaking in public lobbies.

content_raw: Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests. The YouTuber has been an outspoken advocate against Call of Duty's SBMM and has tried to make noise on the issue in a variety of ways. Last week, he began tweeting at Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about the matter every day in hopes of getting her attention. Now, he's trying a different way. After seeing Destiny fans successfully rally together to get Bungie to resurrect the sci-fi MMO, Tdawgsmitty decided to try to bring Call of Duty fans together in hopes of a similar outcome. The YouTuber launched a petition which has gained over 500 signatures in roughly an hour. The call to action aims to get SBMM entirely removed from Call of Duty's unranked lobbies, citing frustrations with the current system and how Activision uses data analysts to develop its matchmaking. Instead, he wants the series to utilize SBMM in the game's ranked play, where players deliberately choose to have a more competitive experience. "Former Call of Duty developer Brian Bright recently shared that his team’s work on [the canceled Call of Duty game NX1] focused on ping and region," reads the description for the petition. "He also stated that Activision eventually began hiring data scientists who worked with its marketing department to push for more skill-based matchmaking. His statement raises serious questions about how matchmaking priorities evolved. "For players like us, today’s public matches too often feel like the same competitive experience on repeat. Experimenting with a different weapon, relaxing after work, or playing with friends of different skill levels can become frustrating. When every lobby feels like another test, the fun starts to disappear." The YouTuber also asked for clearer communication regarding matchmaking and the opportunity for the community to test changes itself. The petition comes roughly a month ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release, which will utilize a divisive SBMM system that was introduced earlier this summer in Black Ops 7. Some feel that Call of Duty's SBMM is too punishing and can result in matches that feel consistently unfair, leading to years of frustrations about the franchise's multiplayer. Whether a petition can change the mind of Activision remains to be seen, but it's not entirely out of the question. Bungie opted to return to Destiny 2 after killing it earlier this year. There was extreme backlash to the initial decision and players decided to make their voices heard through online protests, which included players choosing to not support Bungie's latest game, Marathon. The developer announced that it will be restoring vaulted content and plans to keep supporting the Destiny franchise, leading to an enthusiastic response from fans .
